To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monocrotaline-pyrrole alters DNA, mRNA and protein synthesis in porcine pulmonary endothelial cells.

the effects of monocrotal pyrrole (a toxic pyrrole found in the poisonous plant, rattle snake grass) on pulmonary vascular endothelial cells include: 1) reduced cell division and 2) increased DNA, RNA, protein synthesis.
monocrotaline-treated pulmonary endothelial cells continue to syn-thesize DNA, RNA, protein and maintain cellular activity but the cellular activity is altered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of monocrotalines on pulmonary vascular endothelium and the mechanisms involved.
the effects of MCTP, a pneumotoxicant, on the synthesis of DNA, RNA and proteins in cultured pulmonary artery endothelial (PEC) cells.
the cellular activity of pulmonary vascular endothelial cells treated with monocrotaline.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MCTP-treated endothelial cells are not dead, but are metabolically altered.
the cellular activities of MCTP treated cells are altered in a time- and concentration-dependent manner.
MCTP-treated pulmonary artery endothelial cell cultures continue to synthesize macromolecules, but at a rate and with a quality that is altered from normal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCTP alters the cellular activity of pulmonary artery endothelial cell in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
MCTP-treated endothelial cells remain viable but are altered in morphology and function.
MCTP is a pneumotoxicant which affects the cellular activity and function of pulmonary artery endothelial (PAE) cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cellular activity of endothelial cells is altered substantially by exposure to the pneumotoxicant, monocrotaline.
MCTP exposure results in a reduction of cell proliferation, but the cells continue to divide and synthesize RNA and protein.
MCTP-treated endothelial cells continue to synthezize DNA, RNA, protein and proliferate, although at a reduced rate.
